newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley sued, employees allege bias.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley sued, employees allege bias.

text.p: Two black employees of Morgan Stanley Group Inc. have filed a $60 million race discrimination suit against the company, the company said Monday.
The case stems from an incident in October 1995, when an electonic mailing that included a series of racist jokes was transmitted to a group of Morgan Stanley employees.

According to the suit, which was filed in New York last month and names Morgan Stanley and seven employees as defendants, plaintiffs Yolanda Owens and Edward Hutton allege they were passed over for promotions after complaining about the mailing.

In a statement commenting on the complaint, Morgan Stanley denied discriminating against Owens and Hutton, saying it "immediately launched a full internal investigation" after learning about the incident.
The firm also said employees identified as participants were "severely disciplined" and any with supervisory roles were stripped of their managerial responsibilities.

Where the document originated is a matter of some dispute. The suit alleges a Morgan Stanley employee wrote and sent the message, using the computer identification of a third black employee as a cover. Other employees named as defendants forwarded the message to co-workers, the complaint states.
According to Morgan Stanley's version of the incident, the document "was transmitted into the firm and was forwarded among a small group of employees."

According to court documents provided by Shafran & Mosley, the New York law firm representing the plaintiffs, Owens and Hutton are each seeking $5 million in compensatory damages and $25 million in punitive damages.
The two continue to work for Morgan Stanley, but both are currently on voluntary leave, the firm said.
Morgan Stanley's stock fell $1 to $54.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
